text_blocks.snippet: Active scams targeting Central Illinois residents include fake text messages, spoofed phone calls, and deceptive home repair schemes.

list.snippet: DMV and Toll Text Scams: Scammers send text messages claiming you owe money for unpaid tolls or traffic tickets, threatening license suspension if you do not click a link. The Illinois Secretary of State never sends text messages requesting payment.

Phone Spoofing: Con artists fake the phone numbers of official organizations, such as the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois, demanding immediate payment or personal information.
Utility Slamming: Callers pose as energy choice providers to trick businesses and schools into changing or sharing current rate details.
Garage Door Repair Schemes: Transient operators use search engine manipulation to promote fake local repair services, upcharge for parts, or damage equipment.
Hang up and verify: Do not trust caller ID. Look up the official phone number of the agency or business yourself to confirm if a request is real.
Do not click links: Never open links or reply to unsolicited texts about tolls, traffic fines, or deliveries.
Check credentials: Verify contractors through local registries and demand physical addresses or valid local licensing before paying for home services.

text_blocks.snippet: If you want to report a specific incident or need advice on a suspicious message you received, tell me what type of communication you got (text, call, or email) so I can help you report it to the correct authorities.
